findings.description: Every finding, one object each. An empty array is the clean verdict and is the ONLY way to report one; do not add a sentence or a pseudo-finding to say so -- `notes` is where the evidence for it goes. Report every finding you have: the workflow decides how many reach the comment and discloses the rest.

severity.description: BLOCKER = it will break something, or it is a security defect. RISK = plausible breakage you could not confirm from the tree.

path.description: Repository-relative path, exactly as the manifest spells it, with no leading ./ and no line number. The empty string, and only the empty string, means the finding is repo-wide. A backtick, a newline or any other control character in it refuses the finding: the comment renders this field inside an inline code span, so those characters break the comment rather than the path.

line.description: Line number in the PR HEAD file, not a patch offset. 0 when the finding is not line-specific, and always 0 when path is empty. A line past the end of the file costs the finding its severity, so 0 beats a confident wrong number.

message.description: One sentence saying what is wrong and what it breaks, then one imperative clause giving the fix. No severity word, no path, no line number, no markdown bullet: those are separate fields and the comment is assembled from them. Aim for 400 characters; 2000 is the hard limit and a finding over it is refused. A newline is collapsed to a space, and `<!--` or `-->` refuses the finding, because the comment body is assembled line by line and its state marker is an HTML comment.

notes.description: What you examined and found sound, one short line each: name what you looked at and what you concluded, not that you looked. This is required on every review, including one that reports findings. On a clean verdict it is published as the evidence for it, because a clean verdict with nothing behind it cannot be told from a review that never ran; where there are findings it reaches the job log only and the comment carries the findings alone. It is not a place for a finding, a tick against a criterion nobody has to act on, a summary of the change, or a request that someone else verify something.

items.description: One note. No markdown bullet, no heading and no severity word: each is rendered on its own. A newline or any other control character is collapsed to a space. `<!--` or `-->` REFUSES the note, and so does a note over 500 characters: the comment carries a state marker that is an HTML comment, read back out of the raw body, so that text would rewrite what a later run measures. A refusal is SILENT -- nothing in your turn says it happened -- and a review whose every note is refused publishes as having established nothing. Write `an HTML comment` rather than quoting one. Aim for 120 characters.
